predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Mystras and the Laconian core, Monemvasia, Grand Magne (Mani) and Karytaina with the eastern half of its barony: the nucleus of the Despotate

predecessors.name: Principality of Achaea
predecessors.text: Mystras and the Laconian core, Monemvasia, Grand Magne (Mani) and Karytaina with the eastern half of its barony: the nucleus of the Despotate

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Mystras surrendered on 29 May 1460 (30-31 May on the Mystras page) and 'By the end of summer, virtually all Greek cities had submitted'; Corinth, Patras and the northwest had been annexed in 1458

successors.name: Republic of Venice
successors.text: Modon (Methoni), Koroni, Navarino (Venetian from 1417, venetian-modon-and-coron dossier), the Argolid with Argos and the port of Nafplion, which Venice 'kept' after 1461; Mani and Monemvasia came to…

ledger.x: 1349: John VI Kantakouzenos creates the Despotate of the Morea at Mystras for his son Manuel.
1388: Despot Theodore I Palaiologos takes Argos.
11 June 1394: Theodore cedes Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi to Venice, which keeps them.
About 1402: Salona 'fell for a short time into the hands of the Despotate of the Morea'.
1404: Theodore I sells Salona to the Hospitallers.
1417: Theodore II and John VIII invade Achaea.
1418: the Despotate holds Messenia and Elis.
1430: the Despotate takes the rest of the Latin Morea.
1430: the Despotate takes Patras from Venice.
1432: Centurione II Zaccaria dies in Arcadia and his last barony passes to the Despotate.
1444: Athens becomes a tributary of the Despot of the Morea.
1456: the Ottomans end the duchy's tribute to the Morea.
1458: Mehmed II annexes the north of the Morea.
1460: the Despotate of the Morea ends.

wars.name: Byzantine conquest of the Principality of Achaea
wars.outcome: Theodore II and John VIII took Messenia and Elis in 1417-18; Thomas besieged Centurione at Chalandritsa in 1429 and forced the treaty and marriage of 1429/1430; Centurione died in Arcadia in 1432 and the Despotate took his lands.

wars.name: Manuel Kantakouzenos's war with Francesco Sansverino at Gardiki
wars.outcome: Manuel's army of about 1,000 knights and 2,000 infantry was defeated by Sansverino, the bailli of Achaea, in the mid-1370s; no territory changed hands.

wars.name: Ottoman invasion of the Morea of 1446
wars.outcome: Murad II destroyed the Hexamilion wall; Thomas and Constantine 'accepted Murad as lord, agreed to pay tribute, and promised not to rebuild the wall'.

wars.name: Albanian-Greek revolt of 1453-54
wars.outcome: The Albanian and Greek revolt after the fall of Constantinople was put down in October 1454 with Turahan Bey's Ottoman troops, whom the despots had invited; the tribute rose from 10,000 to 12,000 ducats.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Morea
wars.outcome: Mehmed II annexed Corinth, Patras and the northwest in 1458 (the brothers having paid no tribute for three years); Thomas rebelled against Demetrios and the Ottomans in January 1459; Demetrios surrendered Mystras without a fight on 29 May 1460.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened: the Latin-Byzantine frontier with Achaea, the Ottoman marches and the borders between the co-despots are approximate.
